title: Inspect and extend: What a check record means
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/data.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve check and exposureresult types, symptom catalogue, resources, and sample data.
problem: A record is a dated note about an app action, not a diagnosis. Read the types and fixtures, identify where sample checks and symptom choices come from, and mark which information is fictional. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/data.ts` and the related project files: src/exposure.ts; src/data.ts.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to check and exposureresult types, symptom catalogue, resources, and sample data.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: Seeded content is demonstration data; no public-health data source is contacted.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A record is a dated note about an app action, not a diagnosis. Read the types and fixtures, identify where sample checks and symptom choices come from, and mark which information is fictional.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/data.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
